what_this_closes: Lane F of epic #3073 rested on ONE unread GGUF-header scalar: glm_moe_dsa expert_used_count (K). The GPU-server roofline ESTIMATED active-params/token (~32B) and active-bytes/token (~13 GiB) and scales inversely with both. This witness reads the full GLM-5.2 header on a node with a shard resident, pins K=8 and every companion active-set scalar (expert_ffn_len, shared count, dense/MoE layer split, MLA ranks), and DERIVES the routed-expert active stream. It replaces the PENDING(K) in the Lane F note and the ceiling doc's active-set estimates with measured header truth.

tool.command: gguf-dump <shard1>  (llama.cpp gguf-dump; python-gguf 0.18.0 also present on-box)
tool.scope: GGUF header key-value dump only; NO tensor payloads loaded, NO GPU, NO serve
tool.note: The fak estimator q4kdiag -plan-only prints the same K + expert_ffn_len via internal/ggufload.applyMoEExpertCounts (committed: fb7737b36, b6fd400f7), but `go` was not on PATH on the node, so the header was read directly with gguf-dump. Values are the raw header, tool-independent.

header_measured._source: gguf-dump of shard1, verbatim; key prefix is glm-dsa (glm_moe_dsa arch)

active_set_derived._method: header arithmetic only; gated FFN = 3 matrices (gate/up/down) of H x expert_ffn per expert; MoE layers = block_count - leading_dense_block_count

ffn_active_params_per_token.note: MoE FFN active = (K + shared) x 3 x H x expert_ffn x 76 MoE layers; dense = 3 x H x feed_forward_length x 3 dense layers x 3 matrices. This is the FFN portion only.

active_set_derived.active_params_per_token_total_B: ~30-33 (FFN 27.86B measured-derived + MLA attention ~4-6B compressed); CONSISTENT with the prior ~32B ESTIMATE, now anchored to measured K=8
active_set_derived.routed_expert_active_bytes_method: K=8 x per_expert_resident; per_expert = routed_band / 256 = 414.5 GiB / 256 = 1.619 GiB; routed_band (all 256 experts) = monolith - replicated = q4_k 256.50 + q5_k 150.56 + q6_k 7.38 GiB (EP-load-plan witness monolith rows minus the replicated non-expert rows). Equals internal/ggufload.RoutedExpertActiveSet.ActivePerToken (K x RoutedResident/NumExperts).

_correction_2026_07_14.error: The original derivation used the EP-7 ONE-RANK routed band (q4_k 37.07 + q5_k 21.76 + q6_k 1.07 = 59.90 GiB, which holds ~37 of 256 experts on the busiest rank) but labelled it 'all 256 experts' and divided by 256, giving 0.234 GiB/expert (~7x low). The true routed band spans all 256 experts (monolith q4_k 256.50 + q5_k 150.56 GiB, both entirely routed) = 414.52 GiB; 414.52/256 = 1.619 GiB/expert = 59.90/37. Cross-checked: per-expert params 2.869 B x 256 + non-expert 19.4 B = 753.86 B = the witnessed llama-bench total.
_correction_2026_07_14.consequence: Routed active stream at K=8 is 12.95 GiB (not 1.87), so active-bytes/token = 12.95 routed + 19.31 non-expert = ~32 GiB (upper bound). Routed is ~40% of the active stream, NOT ~9% -- the composition finding below is REVERSED (see _correction). Verified against internal/ggufload.RoutedExpertActiveSet.{ActivePerToken,ActiveBytesPerToken}, which computes 12.95 / 32.26 GiB from the header (unit-tested: gguf_glm_active_set_test.go, gguf_glm_quant_sweep_test.go). The header_measured block above is unaffected (K=8 etc. are the verbatim gguf-dump).

finding_active_bytes_composition._corrected_2026_07_14: The headline/implication below were derived from the 0.234 GiB/expert error (see active_set_derived._correction_2026_07_14) and are REVERSED. Corrected finding: routed active stream = 12.95 GiB/token at K=8, which MATCHES the ceiling doc's original ~10 GiB expert-stream estimate (it was about right). active-bytes/token = 12.95 routed + 19.31 non-expert = ~32 GiB, so routed is ~40% of the stream and non-expert ~60% -- SAME ORDER, not 10:1. The estimate's real error was UNDER-counting the non-expert band (~3 GiB assumed vs 19.31 measured), making active-bytes ~2.5x the ~13 GiB estimate. Lever implication: the L5 routed quant-sweep is HIGH leverage (routed = 40% of active bytes), AND compressing the replicated attn/shared/output band (60%) helps -- both matter, contrary to the superseded 'routed helps less' claim.
finding_active_bytes_composition.headline_SUPERSEDED: The routed-expert active stream is ~1.87 GiB/token at K=8 - roughly 5x SMALLER than the ceiling doc's ~10 GiB 'expert stream' estimate. The active-bytes/token is therefore NOT expert-dominated; it is dominated by the replicated high-precision band (attention + shared-expert + dense), measured resident at ~19.3 GiB (q8_0 18.07 + q6_k 0.73 + f32 0.51 GiB, EP-witness ranks_1 replicated rows).
finding_active_bytes_composition.implication_SUPERSEDED: The ceiling doc's active-bytes COMPOSITION (10 GiB expert + 3 GiB replicated) is inverted vs measurement (~1.9 GiB expert + replicated-dominated). Lever priority shifts: quantizing/compressing the attention + shared-expert band buys more single-stream headroom than quantizing the routed experts (the L5 routed quant-sweep helps less than assumed).
finding_active_bytes_composition.honesty_boundary: This witness pins the header scalars and DERIVES the ROUTED-expert active stream exactly. It does NOT measure the total active-bytes/token: the per-token-active fraction of the replicated band (which attention weights actually stream each decode step under MLA absorption, minus the embedding/output table) requires the decode per-op byte trace - the separate box-side witness that is the second half of #3074. Total active-bytes/token remains an UPPER BOUND (~32 GiB) PENDING that trace; only its expert component (12.95 GiB) is closed here.

corrections: routed-expert active stream: ~10 GiB (estimate) -> 12.95 GiB (measured-derived at K=8; the earlier 1.87 GiB in this file was an EP-7-band/256 error, corrected 2026-07-14)
active-bytes/token TOTAL: ~13 GiB (estimate) -> ~32 GiB upper bound (routed 12.95 + non-expert 19.31; estimate under-counted the non-expert band ~3 GiB vs 19.31 measured)

tests.note: The derivation arithmetic (RoutedExpertActiveSet.ActivePerToken = K x RoutedResident/NumExperts) is committed and unit-tested (internal/ggufload/gguf_glm_active_set_test.go); this witness supplies the measured K it consumes.
